reason: Start with the kidney filter to follow what happens to blood and its dissolved substances.
expectation: I expect the nephron to filter some fluid and small substances from the blood, though the result may show only the first stage.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the ureters would build the drainage route, but filtering comes first in the stated process.

effect: The filter passes fluid and small dissolved substances into the tubule while retaining cells and most proteins, so recovery is the next process to follow.
reaction: The contrast between what passes and what remains is clear.
reason: Add the tubule transporters to see how useful substances are recovered from the filtered fluid.
expectation: I expect some dissolved substances to move from the tubule back toward the blood, though I’m unsure which ones will be shown.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would build the drainage route, but I want to follow recovery first.

effect: The tubule recovers glucose and other useful substances into the blood; water recovery is the next stage to follow.
reaction: The explanation that healthy kidneys normally recover almost all filtered glucose makes the transporters' role clearer.
reason: Add the water-permeable tubule to follow water recovery before tracing drainage.
expectation: I expect some water to move from the tubule toward the blood, leaving a more concentrated fluid.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would establish the drainage route, but I want to finish following recovery first.

effect: Water returns to the blood while wastes remain in the tubule, so the remaining fluid is ready to follow into drainage.
reaction: The picture description makes the contrast clear, though it does not explain how water recovery is regulated.
reason: Follow the recovered sample into the urinary drainage route.
expectation: I expect the remaining fluid to become urine and pass toward the ureter and bladder.

alternatives.reason: The ureters also establish drainage, but I want to finish tracing the sample first.

effect: The remaining fluid is shown as urine flowing through a ureter into the bladder, completing the filtering and recovery goal.
reason: Fit the ureters to the kidney pair to build the urinary organs' drainage route.
expectation: I expect the ureters to connect to the kidneys, leaving the bladder to be fitted.

alternatives.reason: The bladder also needs fitting, but the ureters provide the intervening route.

effect: The ureters are fitted to the kidney pair; the bladder remains to be attached.
reaction: The fitting is straightforward, though the picture text adds little detail.
reason: Fit the bladder to complete the urinary drainage assembly; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the bladder to attach to the ureters and kidneys, ready for connection to the body.

effect: The bladder is fitted, completing the kidney-to-bladder drainage assembly; it can now be connected to the body.
reaction: The explanation makes the route clear, though the fitting was predictable.
reason: Connect the urinary organs to the body to pursue the remaining goal; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the kidneys and urinary drainage route to join the body's circulation and existing organs.

effect: The kidneys are now connected to the body's circulation, with ureters leading to the bladder. The remaining goal is complete.
reaction: The final connection is clear, though predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the selective tubule transporters was most worthwhile: the planned picture and explanation distinguish filtration from recovery and make clear that healthy kidneys normally reclaim almost all filtered glucose.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the ureters and bladder felt repetitive after the sample had already been shown draining to the bladder. The ureter fitting's picture text added little detail.

surprise.text: The emphasis that almost all filtered glucose is normally recovered clarified how much useful material is reclaimed after filtration.

arbitrary.text: No action lacked a clear purpose, but separately fitting the urinary route felt somewhat redundant after seeing urine follow that route. The water-recovery picture also left its regulation unexplained.

continue.text: I would be mildly interested in continuing: the filter-and-recovery sequence made a useful distinction, although the later fittings were predictable.
